mainEntity.name: Who are the best Web3 PR agencies in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Web3 PR market in 2026 splits into two camps. Traditional agencies running multi-person account teams: Lunar Strategy (Lisbon, growth-plus-PR), EAK Digital (long-established, deep Tier-1 trade relationships), Coinbound (US-led integrated marketing), Outset PR (boutique Tier-1 announcement specialists), High Vibe PR (visible across listicle search results). Fractional senior-operator alternatives: Shilika Jain (APAC-native, AI and Web3, $5K to $12K monthly with founder-direct access). The right pick depends on stage, scope, and whether you need a five-person team or one senior operator. There is no single best — there is a best fit for your stage.

mainEntity.name: How much do Web3 PR agencies charge in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Web3 PR agency retainers in 2026 range from $15,000 to $60,000 per month depending on the firm and scope. Mid-tier specialists (Lunar, EAK, Outset) typically run $15,000 to $30,000 monthly. Larger integrated firms (Coinbound, broader marketing agencies with crypto desks) run $25,000 to $50,000 monthly. Boutique fractional senior operators sit at $5,000 to $12,000 monthly for equivalent Tier-1 scope, because there is no five-person account team to fund. Single-launch sprints across any of these models run $15,000 to $40,000.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a Web3 PR agency and a fractional Web3 PR consultant?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Web3 PR agency assigns a multi-person account team (typically an account executive, account manager, account director, and senior partner) at a retainer that funds all four roles. A fractional Web3 PR consultant is one senior operator embedded directly with the founder, with no team layer. The agency model wins on bandwidth (20-plus simultaneous accounts, 24-hour war-room coverage) and adjacent functions (in-house IR, government affairs, analyst relations). The fractional model wins on cost (40 to 60 percent cheaper for equivalent scope), founder access (direct line, same operator day 1 and day 180), and speed to first placement (2 to 4 weeks versus 4 to 8 weeks).

mainEntity.name: How should a Web3 founder choose between agencies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Five questions narrow the field quickly. First, what stage are you? Pre-seed through Series A skews fractional; Series B and beyond can absorb agency overhead productively. Second, how many simultaneous markets do you need? Six or fewer fits fractional; more than six tilts agency. Third, what is your monthly burn rate for comms? Below $15,000 monthly fits fractional; above $25,000 monthly fits agency. Fourth, do you need senior time or team execution hours? Senior-only is fractional; 60-plus execution hours weekly is agency. Fifth, do you need adjacent functions like investor relations or government affairs? If yes, agency. If no, fractional.

mainEntity.name: Who is the best PR consultant for AI startups in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best PR consultant for an AI startup in 2026 is the one whose recent placements match the outlets that matter for AI category creation: Forbes (Cloris Chen and AI Council bylines), AI Magazine, The Information, Decrypt AI, Bloomberg Tech, and named beat reporters at TechCrunch and Wired. Few generalist crypto agencies have these relationships. Shilika Jain placed Gaia AI as the Stripe for AI agents in Forbes (December 2024), Decrypt, and Benzinga inside a single news cycle, anchored to Consensus Hong Kong. The named-outlet placement stack matters more than the agency brand.

mainEntity.name: Are listicle articles ranking Web3 PR agencies trustworthy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most listicles ranking Web3 PR agencies are written by SEO content shops that have no operational view of the category and rank firms by who paid for placement or by superficial criteria like website traffic. The trustworthy listicles disclose their criteria (cost, Tier-1 placement count, regional coverage, named operators), name the trade-offs honestly, and include both their own firm and competitors with comparison. This piece is written by Shilika Jain, an operator inside the category; the conflict of interest is disclosed and so is the methodology.
